findings.reason: The protected source is already the direct optimal parity solution: toggle each character's membership in an odd-frequency set, then accept exactly when that set has at most one member. The state and palindrome criterion are immediately visible, naming is clear, and no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies paid-only LeetCode problem 266 and its Python string contract. The Reference preserves the permutation question, nonempty lowercase-English domain, length limit, and all three factual examples; the contract now defines n and distinct-character count k for the branch bounds.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064289557. It and the app-local source have identical odd-set initialization, membership branch, removal and insertion updates, full character scan, and final cardinality test; only the set annotation and LeetCode wrapper differ.

The previous benchmark violated both source constraints by using thousands of distinct Unicode characters and length 16,384. The legal 32/96/320 tiers use only lowercase English letters with paired counts. The current source passes at +0.01 relative exponent and 1.01x largest ratio; a correct per-position full recount passes every output but fails only scaling at +1.37 and 198.34x.

The Approach proves the odd-frequency invariant and palindrome criterion, now states expected hash-set time, defines O(k) storage under k <= 26, and distinguishes the defensive empty-input result from the native nonempty contract.

The hash-bound paid-only Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving all three examples in order, their lack of source explanations, both constraints, and the zero-visual structure.

coverage: all three source-fidelity-verified strings now appear first and in source order as visible samples with exact Boolean outputs
the former empty-string row was removed because the verified source requires length at least one
one-character and two-character rows cover the legal minimum, the smallest even palindrome, and the smallest false result
letters a and z exercise both ends of the lowercase alphabet without adding source-illegal normalization behavior
aabb is not itself a palindrome but has an all-even permutation, directly distinguishing permutation feasibility from original string order
aabbc verifies the single allowable odd-frequency center, while code and az reject four and two odd frequencies respectively
two copies of every lowercase letter reach the exact 26-character distinct-key bound with all frequencies even
an alternating a/z string reaches the exact 5,000-character maximum with independently verified even counts
all ten expectations matched an independent Counter-based parity oracle, and every authored string through length eight also matched exhaustive permutation enumeration
10,000 seeded random legal lowercase strings matched the independent parity oracle
the protected current source passed all ten correctness rows and all three unchanged benchmark tiers through the real-test engine; benchmark outputs and runtime scaling passed
all ten correctness rows are visible samples or trials, while the unchanged 32, 96, and 320-character inputs remain hidden performance-only benchmarks
